en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya meets Senior Officials of the Russian Embassy
en.description: 11 July 2014, Colombo; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon and Attorney General, His Excellency Mr. Mohamed Anil has today met with the Senior Officials of the Russian Embassy regarding Seleznyov's arrest.
en.body:
11 July 2014, Colombo; Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon and Attorney General, His Excellency Mr. Mohamed Anil has today met with the Senior Officials of the Russian Embassy regarding Seleznyov's arrest.

At the meeting held today at the Maldives High Commission in Sri Lanka, both the Foreign Minister and Attorney General of Maldives explained to the Russian officials that Maldives had followed past practices in dealing with Interpol red notices. Minister Dunya also briefed the incident report of the case and answered to questions raised

Minister Dunya also noted the close bilateral relations between Maldives and Russia, and conversed that the President of Maldives, His Excellency Mr Yameen Abdul Gayoom is working to further strengthen the existing ties. Minister added that the bilateral ties between two countries are much stronger and would not hinder the close relationship surrounding the arrest of Seleznyov.

The two parties also discussed on entering into agreements in order to avoid such incidents in the future.

ENDS

en.title: President of Maldives condemns Israeli aggression in Palestine
en.description: 10 July 2014, Male'; President of Maldives, Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has condemned the continued Israeli aggression and the gross violation of human rights in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. The President describes the aggressions as a deliberate massacre of innocent civilians by Israel. The…
en.body:
10 July 2014, Male'; President of Maldives, Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has condemned the continued Israeli aggression and the gross violation of human rights in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. The President describes the aggressions as a deliberate massacre of innocent civilians by Israel. The President notes that Maldivians empathize with the suffering that our Palestinian brothers and sisters are enduring during the holy month of Ramadan.

President Yameen calls on Israel to bring an immediate end to the airstrikes; an end the incursions; and end to the degrading and inhuman treatment of the Palestinians. The President also calls Israel to start recognising and respecting Palestinian rights, particularly the fundamental human rights of the Palestinian people. The President urges Israel to lift the blockade; to dismantle the wall, and the illegal settlement; and to return to the negotiation table. It is only through negotiations that a conducive environment could be created where both Palestine and Israel could live side by side in peace.

ENDS.

en.title: Temporary Closure of the University of Science and Technology Chittagong (USTC) in Bangladesh
en.description: 10 July 2014, Male';The Government of Maldives has been liaising closely with the Government of Bangladesh, in seeking a solution to the pressing issues faced by Maldivian students, due to the temporary closure of the University of Science and Technology Chittagong (USTC) in Bangladesh.
en.body:
10 July 2014, Male';The Government of Maldives has been liaising closely with the Government of Bangladesh, in seeking a solution to the pressing issues faced by Maldivian students, due to the temporary closure of the University of Science and Technology Chittagong (USTC) in Bangladesh.

The Government of Maldives has been informed that the Government of Bangladesh is working with relevant authorities to ensure that the situation is resolved at the earliest, so that the students can resume their studies.

ENDS.

en.title: Press Release of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
en.description: 9 July 2014; The Maldives is a member of the Interpol since 1984 and follows a practice of enforcing Red Notices issued by the international organization.
en.body:
9 July 2014; The Maldives is a member of the Interpol since 1984 and follows a practice of enforcing Red Notices issued by the international organization.

Most recently the Government of Maldives has given effect to such a Red Notice on 5 July 2014 in locatinga Russian national in the country who had been wanted by the Interpol. The Government of Maldives followed its past practice in dealing with the matter.

End.

en.title: New High Commissioner of Seychelles calls on Foreign Minister
en.description: 07 July 2014, Male'; His Excellency Mr. Waven William, new High Commissioner of the Republic of Seychelles to the Republic of Maldives has called on Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives.
en.body:
07 July 2014, Male'; His Excellency Mr. Waven William, new High Commissioner of the Republic of Seychelles to the Republic of Maldives has called on Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives.

At the meeting held at the Foreign Ministry this afternoon, Minister welcomed the High Commissioner and congratulated him on his appointment. Foreign Minister noted that as Small Island developing states the Maldives and Seychelles share a number of common concerns including the adverse effects of climate change, and discussed ways of further strengthening the close bilateral relations between the two countries and working closely together on issues on common interest.

The High Commissioner assured his commitment to working with the Government of Maldives in strengthening the relations between the two countries and in bringing issues of common concern to the international forefront.

Foreign Minister was accompanied by Ms. Fathimath Inaya, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Ms. Fathimath Najwa, Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS.

en.title: New Finnish Ambassador calls on the Foreign Minister
en.description: 07 July 2014, Male'; The new Ambassador of Finland to the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Mr. Rauli Suikkanen has called on the Foreign Minister, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon.
en.body:
07 July 2014, Male'; The new Ambassador of Finland to the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Mr. Rauli Suikkanen has called on the Foreign Minister, Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon.

At the meeting held at the Foreign Ministry this afternoon, the Foreign Minister welcomed the Ambassador and congratulated him on his appointment. Foreign Minister also noted the close bilateral relations between the Maldives and Finland, and discussed ways of further strengthening the existing ties, especially in sectors such as tourism and investment promotion.

The Ambassador assured his commitment to working with the Government in strengthening the relations between the two countries and assured Finland's cooperation in the development of the Maldives.

Foreign Minister Dunya was accompanied by Ms. Fathimath Inaya, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Mr. Hussain Jahhaz, Senior Desk Officer of the Foreign Ministry of the Maldives.

ENDS.

en.title: New Finnish Ambassador presents credentials to the President
en.description: 07 July 2014, Male'; The new Ambassador of Finland accredited to the Maldives, H. E. Rauli Suikkanen presented his letter of credence to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this morning.
en.body:
07 July 2014, Male'; The new Ambassador of Finland accredited to the Maldives, H. E. Rauli Suikkanen presented his letter of credence to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this morning.

At the ceremony held at the President's Office to present credentials, President Yameen welcomed Ambassador Suikkanen to the Maldives, and congratulated the Ambassador on the commencement of his term.

Meeting the new Ambassador afterwards, the President and the ‎Ambassador discussed bilateral relations that exist between the two ‎countries and ways to further strengthen ties.‎

Noting the similarities between the Maldives and Finland, President Yameen and Ambassador Suikkanen exchanged ideas on areas of mutual concern. In this regard, discussions were focused on the efforts being made in both countries in advocating human rights, empowering women, and strengthening democracy.

‎The meeting was attended by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, and Minister at the President's Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef.

ENDS.

en.title: "The celebration of the Fourth of July is not just a celebration of an anniversary but a celebration of freedom, liberty, and justice" says Foreign Minister Dunya
en.description: 07 July 2014, Male'; Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon made these remarks attending the reception held to commemorate the 238th anniversary of the Independence of the United States of America.
en.body:
07 July 2014, Male'; Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon made these remarks attending the reception held to commemorate the 238th anniversary of the Independence of the United States of America.

Speaking at the reception, Minister Dunya conveyed warm greetings and good wishes on behalf of the President Yameen and remarked that the celebration of the Fourth of July is not just a celebration of an anniversary but a celebration of freedom, liberty, and justice.

Minister underscored that the declaration of independence was first signed in 1776 by the founding fathers, the United States has become a beacon of hope for millions around the world.

Furthermore, the Minister stated that the United States is a close and trusted partner of the Maldives and next year would mark the Golden Jubilee of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Maldives and the United States. She also highlighted that Maldives will continue to work with the US in suppressing terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, organized crimes, drug trafficking, and other security issues.

Minister expressed appreciation for the assistance and cooperation from the United States in field of defence and security, particularly for the continued training through Joint Military Exercises.

Minister also thanked Ambassador Sisson and Embassy staff who have monitored and assisted the Maldives in its efforts to stop Human Trafficking.

Concluding the speech Minister expressed sincere appreciation to the Government of the United States for the continued support, engagement and assistance towards the progress of the nation.

ENDS

en.title: The Maldives' plays a proactive role in the 26th Session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: 27 June 2014, Geneva;The 26th session of the UN Human Rights Council has concluded today. The Maldives as a member of the council participated actively in the debates and the negotiations on a number of key human rights issues during the session.
en.body:
27 June 2014, Geneva;The 26th session of the UN Human Rights Council has concluded today. The Maldives as a member of the council participated actively in the debates and the negotiations on a number of key human rights issues during the session.

The Maldives was in the core group of two key resolutions namely ‘mandate of the Independence of Judges and Lawyers' and ‘The contribution of parliaments to the work of the Human Rights Council and its Universal Periodic Review', which were adopted by consensus. The Maldives co-sponsored 14 resolutions including ‘Accelerating efforts to eliminate violence against women', ‘Elimination of discrimination against women', ‘Human Rights and Climate Change' and ‘Mandate of the Special Rapporteur on trafficking of persons, especially women and children'. The Maldives was in the core-group which led the high level panel, ‘Power of Empowered Women 2014' with the participation of inspiring women leaders and entrepreneurs from around the world in a global conversation on equality and women's economic empowerment.

The Maldives engaged in important debates on the situation of human rights in the Syrian Arab Republic, Palestine and the DPRK. During the Interactive Dialogue with the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Syrian Arab Republic, the Maldives condemned all parties of the conflict which had has led to the death of over 160,000 people and displacement of millions of civilians. The Maldives also expressed concern about the systematic, widespread and gross violations of human rights in North Korea, at the refusal of the Government of North Korea to effectively address the violations in the country, and to immediately ensure that fundamental freedoms and liberties are afforded to its citizens.The Maldives further condemned the gross human rights violation of the rights of Palestinian people and expansion of illegal settlements by Israel, the occupying power.

A total of 40 resolutions were adopted during this session of the UN Human Rights Council and a number of key human rights issues were debated. The Maldives was represented at the session by the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Maldives to the United Nations Offices in Geneva.

ENDS

en.title: President of Sri Lanka concludes State Visit to the Maldives
en.description: 27 June 2014, Male'; President of Sri Lanka, Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady ‎Shiranthi Rajapaksa, have concluded their state visit to the Maldives. The ‎Sri Lankan President and First Lady were seen off at the Malé ‎International Airport by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dunya Maumoon. ‎
en.body:
27 June 2014, Male'; President of Sri Lanka, Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady ‎Shiranthi Rajapaksa, have concluded their state visit to the Maldives. The ‎Sri Lankan President and First Lady were seen off at the Malé ‎International Airport by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dunya Maumoon. ‎

During the visit, President Rajapaksa called on President Abdulla ‎Yameen Abdul Gayoom and held official talks between both ‎Governments.‎

Three important agreements were signed between the ‎Government of Maldives and Sri Lanka during the visit. The three ‎agreements signed were, MoU on Health Cooperation; MoU on ‎Strengthening cooperation between Board of Investment of Sri Lanka and ‎Ministry of Economic Development of Maldives, and the agreement for ‎Arrangement on Search and Rescue

President Yameen and First Lady Fathimath Ibrahim hosted a ‎State banquet in honour of the Sri Lankan President and First Lady.‎

ENDS.

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya calls on President of Sri Lanka
en.description: 26 June 2014, Male'; Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon calls on His Excellency Mahinda Rajapaksa, President of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka.
en.body:
26 June 2014, Male'; Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon calls on His Excellency Mahinda Rajapaksa, President of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka.

At the meeting held at Kurumba Maldives this morning, Minister Dunya welcomed the President to the Maldives and extended good wishes from the Government and the People of the Republic of Maldives. Minister noted the close bilateral relations between the Maldives and Sri Lanka, and discussed ways of further strengthening the existing ties between the countries.

During the meeting, Minister Dunya highlighted the MoUs that were signed during President Rajapaksa's visit and emphasized on the urgent need to strengthen the health sector of the Maldives. She also expressed confidence that the MoUs signed in other areas including search and rescue and strengthening of cooperation between the Ministry of Economic Development and the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka will further strengthen the closeness and cooperation between the two countries.

Further, Minister discussed the close cooperation that exists in the regional and international arena. She also mentioned and discussed ways of strengthening the newly established Foreign Service Institute of Maldives.

Minister Dunya was accompanied by H.E. Dr. Ali Naseer Mohamed, Foreign Secretary, H.E. Abdulla Hameed, Ambassador at-Large, H.E. Dr. Mohamed Asim, Ambassador at-Large, Ms. Fathimath Inaya, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Ms. Zahiya Zareer, High Commissioner-designate to Sri Lanka from Maldives, and Dr. Aishath Shehenaz, Additional Secretary.

ENDS

en.title: Remarks by Her Excellency Ms Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives on the State visit of His Excellency Mahindha Rajapaksa, President of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka , 26 June 2014
en.description: Bismillahi Rahmani Raheem Ladies and Gentlemen, Assalaamu Alaikum and good morning
en.body:
Bismillahi Rahmani Raheem

Ladies and Gentlemen, Assalaamu Alaikum and good morning

Yesterday marked yet another important step in the relationship between the Maldives and Sri Lanka. The visit of His Excellency President Mahinda Rajapaksa is an important milestone for several reasons: It is the first visit by a Head of State to the Maldives, since the Government of President Abdullah Yameen took office and the fifth official visit by President Rajapaksa. Sri Lanka is one of our oldest and closest friends.

Sri Lanka was among the first countries to establish relations with the Maldives. We established formal ties on the very first day the Maldives gained independence, on 26 July 1965. Next year, we will mark the Golden Jubilee of our relationship. This long-standing relationship and the mutual trust and respect that exist between our two countries, has made Sri Lanka, a life-long friend of the Maldives.

People-to-people contact between our two countries is exemplary. It is helping the economies of our two countries. The Maldives benefits from the large number of Sri Lankans working in various sectors in the country. The Maldives, in its own way, also helps economic growth in Sri Lanka. Last year, more than 80,000 Maldivian tourists visited Sri Lanka. Maldives is the fourth largest source market for Sri Lankan tourism. We recognize and applaud the tremendous post-conflict reconstruction efforts of the Sri Lankan Government. We believe that the Sri Lankan Government and its people can address and overcome the challenges of post-conflict reconstruction and rehabilitation.

Similarly, we are confident that Sri Lanka will soon be able to overcome challenges arising from the tensions that flared up between Muslims and Buddhists in some parts of Sri Lanka in the recent weeks. Peace and stability is vital for any country or community.

Since 1906, long before formal relations were established, the Maldives maintained a mission in Sri Lanka. Similarly, we regard the presence of Sri Lanka in the Maldives, a matter of utmost importance. Therefore, we are pleased to announce, on a reciprocal basis, allocation of land to build the chancery of the High Commission of Sri Lanka in the Maldives.

This visit has cemented the strong relationship that exists between our two countries. Yesterday, our two countries signed three agreements, including on health cooperation. Maldivians have been long standing consumers of the excellent education and health services in Sri Lanka. Under the agreement signed yesterday, the Maldives looks forward to further enhancing cooperation in the health sector, including in investing in human resources, recruitment of medical doctors and health professionals, and procurement of pharmaceuticals. Under the agreement, we would receive the services of at least three specialists per year, and five seats for Maldivian students to study for MBBS. We also signed agreements on Search & Rescue and strengthening economic investments.

The Maldives and Sri Lanka will continue to cooperate on a variety of issues of mutual importance. This will be further facilitated through the continuation of the discussions of the Joint Commission, which Sri Lanka has graciously agreed to host later this year.

I am pleased that the visit of President Rajapaksa, has been a tremendous milestone in the relationship between our two countries, our Governments and our people.

Thank you.

en.title: President and First Lady host state banquet in honour of visiting Sri Lankan President and First Lady.
en.description: 25 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Fathimath Ibrahim have hosted a State banquet in honour of the visiting President of Sri Lanka, Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa. The banquet was held this evening at Kurumba Maldives.
en.body:
25 June 2014, Male'; President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Fathimath Ibrahim have hosted a State banquet in honour of the visiting President of Sri Lanka, Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa. The banquet was held this evening at Kurumba Maldives.

The national anthems of Maldives and Sri Lanka were played at the banquet.

The banquet was attended by Vice President, Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed and Madam Khawlath Faheem. Chief Justice, Cabinet Ministers, Members of the Parliament, and foreign diplomats were also in attendance at the function, along with the members of the Sri Lankan delegation.

ENDS.

en.title: First Lady Fathimath ‎Ibrahim ‎meets Sri Lankan First Lady
en.description: 25 June 2014, Male'; First Lady, Madam Fathimath Ibrahim has today met with First Lady of Sri Lanka, Madam Shiranthi Rajapaksa.
en.body:
25 June 2014, Male'; First Lady, Madam Fathimath Ibrahim has today met with First Lady of Sri Lanka, Madam Shiranthi Rajapaksa.

At the meeting held at Mulee-aage, discussions were focused ‎on the respective charity work of the two First Ladies. They also ‎exchanged views on improving the rights of Maldivian children with ‎special needs.

ENDS.

en.title: Important agreements signed between the Governments of Maldives and Sri Lanka
en.description: 25 June 2014, Male'; Three very important agreements were signed today between the Governments of Maldives and Sri Lanka. The ceremony was held at the President's Office this evening.
en.body:
25 June 2014, Male'; Three very important agreements were signed today between the Governments of Maldives and Sri Lanka. The ceremony was held at the President's Office this evening.

Following are the agreements that were signed:

1. MoU on Health Cooperation

The agreement was signed by Minister of Health, Dr. Maryam Shakeela, and Sri Lankan Minister of External Affairs, Hon. G. L. Peiris.

2. MoU on Strengthening cooperation between Board of Investment of Sri Lanka and Ministry of Economic Development of Maldives

The agreement was signed by Minister of Economic Development, Hon. Mohamed Saeed, and Sri Lankan Minister of External Affairs, Hon. G. L. Peiris.

3. Arrangement on Search and Rescue

The agreement was signed by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, and Sri Lankan Minister of External Affairs, Hon. G. L. Peiris.

President Yameen and President Mahinda Rajapaksa were in attendance at the signing ceremony.

ENDS.

en.title: Maldives and Sri Lanka hold official talks
en.description: 25 June 2014, Male'; The Government of Maldives and Sri Lanka have held official talks, led by President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and the Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa.
en.body:
25 June 2014, Male'; The Government of Maldives and Sri Lanka have held official talks, led by President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and the Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa.

The President reiterated the government's commitment to enhance the welfare of the people, develop and diversify the economy, strengthen social cohesion within the country, and empower the youth.

At the meeting, discussions were also held on the regional and international issues of mutual concern.

en.title: President of Sri Lanka arrives in the Maldives on a State Visit
en.description: 25 June 2014, Male'; At the invitation of President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Fathimath Ibrahim, President Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa of Sri Lanka have arrived in the Maldives this afternoon. The Sri Lankan President and First Lady were greeted on arrival…
en.body:
25 June 2014, Male'; At the invitation of President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Fathimath Ibrahim, President Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa of Sri Lanka have arrived in the Maldives this afternoon. The Sri Lankan President and First Lady were greeted on arrival at the Ibrahim Nasir International Airport, by President Yameen and Madam Fathimath Ibrahim.

Later, on arrival at the Malé Official Jetty, President Rajapaksa and Madam Shiranthi Rajapaksa were greeted by Vice President Dr. Mohamed Jameel Ahmed and his spouse Hawlath Faheem.

A bugle call was sounded on arrival of the Sri Lankan President and First Lady, after which President Yameen accompanied the visiting President to the saluting dais and a 21-Gun Salute was offered; followed by which the national anthems of Maldives and Sri Lanka were played. President Rajapaksa then proceeded to inspect a Guard of Honour by the Maldives National Defence Force.

At the ceremony, President Rajapaksa was introduced to Ministers, and other senior officials of the Maldives' Government. The members of the Sri Lankan delegation were then introduced to President Yameen.

ENDS.

23 June 2014, Male'; President Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Shiranthi ‎Rajapaksa of Sri Lanka will arrive in the Maldives on Wednesday, 25th ‎June, on a State Visit. The Sri Lankan President is to make this State ‎Visit at the invitation of President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, ‎extended earlier this year during his State Visit to Sri Lanka.‎

President Rajapaksa will be accompanied by an official ‎delegation comprising of Cabinet Ministers, Members of Parliament ‎and other senior Sri Lankan government officials. During his visit to ‎the Maldives, President Rajapaksa is scheduled to meet with President ‎Yameen to discuss bilateral ties between the two countries. High level ‎talks will be held at the President's Office between delegations of both ‎countries. President Yameen will also host a state banquet in honour of ‎the President and First Lady of Sri Lanka. ‎

The Sri Lankan President is the first Head of State, or Head of ‎Government, to make a State Visit to the Maldives since the ‎assumption of presidential office by President Yameen.‎

en.body:
20 June 2014, Male': Foreign Minister Dunya Maumoon has returned to Maldives, concluding her visit to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, to attend the 41st Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).

Minister Dunya delivered a statement at the Meeting in which she highlighted that Islamic principles, values of justice and equality of all humans are in line with modern democratic values. She also spoke about the deep impact Islam had on the rights of women and called on the OIC to work to safeguard women's rights around the world.

The 41st Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the OIC was held in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The Foreign Ministers of the fifty-seven member organization discussed ways in addressing some of the major challenges facing the Islamic Ummah, under the theme "exploring areas of Islamic Cooperation".Minister Dunya was accompanied by His Excellency Mr. Abdullah Hameed, Ambassador-at-large at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ms. Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Assistant Director at the Ministry.

en.description: 20 June 2014, Male': Minister of Foreign Affairs Ms Dunya Maumoon has said that "upgrading the Maldives to Tier 2 level in the Trafficking in Persons Report is a vindication of the Government's policies on stopping human trafficking in the Maldives". en.body:
20 June 2014, Male': Minister of Foreign Affairs Ms Dunya Maumoon has said that "upgrading the Maldives to Tier 2 level in the Trafficking in Persons Report is a vindication of the Government's policies on stopping human trafficking in the Maldives". The Minister made the remarks in response to the decision by the United States to upgrade the Maldives to "Tier 2" level from last year's "Tier 2 Watch List" in the 2014 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report prepared by the US State Department. The Report was released by United States Secretary of State Mr John Kerry today at a ceremony held at the State Department. The Maldives Ambassador to the United States, Mr Ahmed Sareer also attended the ceremony.

The Minister further said that "the decision by the authors of the Report to elevate the Maldives' position is one further indication of the strong acceptance there is for the President's policies'. The Minister also recognized the vital role that the People's Majlis played in enacting the necessary legislations to combat human trafficking in the Maldives. The Minister said that the Maldives would study the recommendations contained in the Report and emphasized the importance of fully implementing the Government's strategic action plan on human trafficking in the Maldives.

The Minister also emphasized the pivotal role that the Foreign Ministry has been playing in raising awareness about human trafficking, and in working with national and international stakeholders in tackling the issue. The Foreign Ministry, under the leadership of the then Foreign Minister, the late Dr Abdul Samad Abdullah, launched a ‘blue-ribbon campaign" in January 2013 aimed at raising awareness on the issue.
